title: Lightboard 1:1 cadence scratch — Ezra Lam
content:
Purpose: quick, focused 30m check-in before the sprint planning review. Keep this light — decisions + unblock > status readout.

Context / recent updates (TL;DR):
- Streaming KV cache rollout to staging completed (canary x3). Latency P95 improved for small requests but p99 spikes on cold-starts persist.
- Oncall rotation caused 2 incidents last week: one SLI regression (INF-3245) and a flaky GPU node in eu-west-1. SRE investigating.
- Hiring: offer accepted for IC3 infra (start mid-Oct). Still need one more infra IC2 to keep on-call coverage sane.

Meeting goals (top 3):
1) Get a firm decision on prioritizing p99 cold-start mitigation vs. continuing canary expansion.
2) Align on headcount ask (one infra IC2 + 0.5 SWE contractor for 2 months) and next steps to present to Lina.
3) Quick career check-in: path to L4 for Priya (concrete next steps + timeline).

Agenda (30m)
- 0–3m: quick personal check-in (energy, focus)
- 3–10m: incident summary (what caused p99, immediate mitigations) — me
- 10–18m: tradeoff discussion: cold-start fixes (kernel preload, lightweight warmers) vs. rollout cadence. Ask: do we pause expansion if p99 > 700ms?
- 18–24m: headcount + resourcing: present ask + risks if we don't hire
- 24–28m: career talk for Priya — agree on 3 deliverables for L4 promotion packet by Nov 1
- 28–30m: recap + action items

Key data points to surface quickly
- Current p95 = 130ms, p99 = 820ms (staging canary). Baseline before cache was p95=210ms, p99=1.6s.
- Cost delta for continuous warmers: +6% infra spend, decreases p99 by ~300ms in naive test.
- Oncall burn: 8.5 extra hours/week across infra team due to current instability.

Decision framing (my recommendation)
- Short term: pause canary expansion for 48–72h and push a lightweight kernel-preload prototype to canary; if p99 improves by >25% move to staged rollout.
- Medium: allocate contractor (6–8w) to implement warmers and safety checks; hire IC2 to absorb oncall load long term.

Questions I want to ask / answers I need from manager
- Would you support a 72h pause on expansion given the SLA risk? (I need explicit yes/no)
- Is the headcount ask feasible in the next hiring slot (can we start requisition this week)?
- What framing would you prefer for the exec-ask (cost vs. reliability)?
- What level of autonomy should Priya have on the kernel-preload RFC? (lead vs. co-lead)

Talking points for upward ask (2–3 lines each)
- Reliability framing: "We can reduce customer-facing p99 by ~40% with a small, bounded infra cost increase; this protects routes with high SLAs and reduces support noise."
- Cost framing: "6% incremental infra cost buys us 300ms lower p99 and avoids churn from repeated incident triage — net savings when factoring SRE time and customer credits."

Notes to self (dont read aloud unless asked)
- Be concise on incidents — avoid deep debugging detail. Offer follow-ups instead.
- If Lina pushes back on hiring, propose a 3-month contractor as compromise.
- Bring up Priya's recent PRs: 2 high-impact PRs (serving-runtime #1178 & #1184) as evidence for promotion readiness.

Prep checklist (before meeting)
- [ ] Snapshot SLO dashboard at 08:00 (p95/p99, error rate) — attach screenshot in follow-up
- [ ] Short demo GIF of kernel-preload test (10s) — show only if asked
- [ ] Draft headcount justification doc (1-pager) — share during meeting
- [ ] One-sentence recommended ask for Lina to send to finance if approved

Action items (to assign in meeting)
- If pause approved: me -> open rollback/hold PR + update canary schedule (today)
- Contractor approval: me -> draft contracting scope + 2 vendor names (by Sep 21)
- Hiring req: manager -> confirm headcount slot and intro to TA (by Sep 22)
- Priya promotion packet: Priya + me -> finalize 3 deliverables + evidence list (by Oct 15)
- Incident deep-dive: SRE -> root-cause draft (INF-3245) (by Sep 20)

Follow-up cadence
- If we pause: quick async update thread in #infra-decisions with data snapshot (I will post)
- Weekly check: 15min sync Wed mornings until canary fully expanded

Random prompts / personal reminders
- Keep tone: factual + collaborative; avoid emotional language about repeated incidents.
- Ask manager for an example blurb to use for exec summary (2 lines).

End of doc — lightweight, can iterate post-meeting for notes + decisions.
